import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_31/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_31/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_31/training_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_31/training_3.csv"
source4_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_31/training_4.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # ['County', 'm1403']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # ['County']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # ['County', 'm1401']
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)  # ['County', 'm1402']
df4 = pd.read_csv(source4_path, index_col=0)  # ['County', 'm1404']

# Step 1: Identify all unique counties from all sources to ensure full coverage
# Union of all counties from all sources
counties_0 = set(df0['County'].unique())
counties_1 = set(df1['County'].unique())
counties_2 = set(df2['County'].unique())
counties_3 = set(df3['County'].unique())
counties_4 = set(df4['County'].unique())

all_counties = counties_0.union(counties_1).union(counties_2).union(counties_3).union(counties_4)

# Create a DataFrame with all counties as base (dimension table)
df_counties = pd.DataFrame({'County': sorted(all_counties)})

# Step 2: Merge all source tables on 'County' to get all m1401, m1402, m1403, m1404 columns
# Left join df_counties with each source table to preserve all counties

df_merged = df_counties.merge(df2, on='County', how='left')  # m1401
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df3, on='County', how='left')    # m1402
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df0, on='County', how='left')    # m1403
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df4, on='County', how='left')    # m1404

# Step 3: Fill missing values in m1401, m1402, m1403, m1404 with 'NR' (as seen in target examples)
for col in ['m1401', 'm1402', 'm1403', 'm1404']:
    if col in df_merged.columns:
        df_merged[col] = df_merged[col].fillna('NR')
    else:
        # If any column is missing (should not happen), create it with 'NR'
        df_merged[col] = 'NR'

# Step 4: The target schema is ['County', 'm1401', 'm1402', 'm1403', 'm1404']
# Ensure columns are in the correct order
df_target = df_merged[['County', 'm1401', 'm1402', 'm1403', 'm1404']]

# Step 5: Export the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_31/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_31/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_31/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_31/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_31/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_31/training_4.csv", index_col=0)

# Join source2 with source3 on County
df = pd.merge(source2, source3, on="County", how="inner")

# Join the result with source0 on County
df = pd.merge(df, source0, on="County", how="inner")

# Join the result with source4 on County
df = pd.merge(df, source4, on="County", how="inner")

# Join the result with source1 on County to filter only counties present in source1
df = pd.merge(df, source1, on="County", how="inner")

# Group by County to ensure uniqueness and remove duplicates if any
df = df.groupby("County", as_index=False).first()

# Write the final output
df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_31/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
